data.name: Celestina
data.long_meaning: Celestina is a Latin name derived from the word celestis, meaning 'heavenly' or 'celestial'. In Christianity, this name is often associated with the Virgin Mary, as she is the one who brought God's grace to earth. Celestina is also the name of several saints, including St. Celestina of Rome, who was a martyr in the 4th century.

data.cultural_impact: The name Celestina has a rich and enduring cultural significance, particularly in the Western world. In literature, Celestina is the title of a novel by Fernando de Rojas, published in 1514, which is considered a classic example of the picaresque novel. The character Celestina in the novel is an old, wise, and powerful woman who uses her knowledge of human nature to manipulate those around her. The name has also been used in music, with songs such as "Celestina" by Mariza, which explores the theme of love and the longing for the divine.
